correctness.rationale: Every vertex coordinate and determinant lies in Z[sqrt(2)]; CHECK.py explicitly enumerates all 10626 quadruples with exact sign comparisons, verifies all 23 determinant-level counts, maximum 32+20sqrt(2) at 48 quadruples, anchored 1771-case symmetry reconstruction, and 16 face/base pairs each with constant signed maximal determinant. Vertex replacement for separately convex absolute determinants extends this to all contained tetrahedra. The exact pyramid decomposition gives polytope volume (96+80sqrt(2))/3; the occupancy simplification follows. The standalone checker was run from the actual science package path; encoded-file integrity and replay after embedding are separately checked at delivery.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches plus full-text inspection of the 2021 primary coordinate source and the three most relevant exact tetrahedral results distinguish both the object and the proved implication. The 24-vertex small rhombicuboctahedron with 8 triangles and 18 squares is not the 48-vertex truncated cuboctahedron, a snub cube, or the cube–octahedron intersection. Exact determinant spectrum, maximal volume, and 16 movable-apex families are not delivered by those papers. Residual historical indexing and an inaccessible reversed-containment presentation are disclosed.
residual_risks: An unindexed classical maximum-inscribed-tetrahedron table or an independently derived determinant spectrum could duplicate this finite exact result.
The original Murphy–Weed PDF could not be visually inspected because the host returned 404; its indexed theorem concerns a different reverse inclusion problem.
No claim is made of an exhaustive characterization of all arbitrary-point maximizing tetrahedra; there may be additional equality sets.

value.rationale: Maximal inscribed tetrahedron volume is a natural sharp scale-free Euclidean invariant of a classical Archimedean solid. The exact 23-level determinant spectrum, 48 vertex maximizers, and 16 explicit two-dimensional non-rigid equality families provide geometric content not recoverable from ordinary volume and facet counts, and the result compares naturally to known maximal-tetrahedron studies in other symmetric 3-polytopes. No universal or large-paper consequence is asserted.
